original_question: Which photoreceptor cells are impacted by the X-linked genetic eye disorder caused by mutations in the gene cluster located at position Xq28, which results in severe color blindness?

final_qi.question: Which photoreceptor cells are impacted by the X-linked genetic eye disorder caused by mutations in the gene cluster located at position Xq28, which results in severe color blindness?
final_qi.long_answer: Mutations in the opsin gene cluster at Xq28 (OPN1LW and OPN1MW) abolish the function of the long- (L, red-sensing) and medium- (M, green-sensing) wavelength cone photoreceptors. Loss of these cones leaves only blue cones and rods active, producing severe X-linked color blindness such as blue-cone monochromacy or protan/deutan deficiencies.

final_answer.long_answer: The X-linked disorder arises from mutations in the OPN1LW/OPN1MW opsin gene cluster at Xq28, which encode the photopigments of long-wave (L, red) and medium-wave (M, green) cone photoreceptors. Loss of these opsins abolishes the function of red and green cone cells, producing the severe colour-vision deficiency characteristic of blue-cone monochromacy.
